answer: Early in the network's dawn, identities were free and sybils swarmed like a nebula of fake agents. The fix: make each identity cost compute. To register, an agent must solve a hash puzzle whose difficulty scales with total registrations and stand on that proof like a ledge. Minting a million fakes burns a million times the energy of one honest agent, and rising difficulty makes late attackers pay exponentially more. Influence follows proof-of-work, not population, so identity farming becomes an energy bill with no return.
